description: One valid example per record type, plus a recall response. These are fixtures: every one validates against its schema, so a builder can use them as golden inputs and a test suite can assert against them. They trace a single realistic story — an agent gets an invoice format wrong, records the failure, learns the fact, and proposes a procedure that a human then approves.

record.content: Sent the March invoice to Acme as a Word document. Client replied asking for PDF with the PO number in the subject line.
record.observation: Client replied within the hour: 'can you resend as PDF, and put the PO number in the subject?'

record.content: Acme requires invoices as PDF with the PO number in the email subject line.

provenance.note: Distilled from a single failed send plus the client's explicit correction.

procedural.note: This is what the record looks like AFTER approval. Before approval the same candidate sits in the `proposals` table and is unreachable by recall.

record.content: Invoicing Acme: export the invoice as PDF, put the PO number in the email subject, cc billing@acme.example. Triggered when sending any invoice to Acme.
preconditions: A PO number exists for the engagement
The invoice has been approved internally

steps.instruction: Export the invoice as PDF, not Word.
Put the PO number in the email subject line, format 'Invoice <ref> — PO <po>'.

record.success_signal: No reply asking for a resend within 2 business days
record.failure_signal: Client replies requesting a different format or a missing PO

approval.rationale: Matches what the client asked for directly. Low risk, three steps, all reversible.

observations.text: Located the March invoice, ref INV-2026-0312.
